_about: Placeable blueprints (owner's spec 30 §§1-9). A blueprint names tag-based ingredient slots, the Construction level and learned skill node it needs, its footprint, the construction workload and the finished station's tags. Completed structures get their level from the level-contributing exact ingredients, clamped by the blueprint and capped by the Construction category level. Values from the historical tutorial (2 Plank Shape + 2 Pillar Shape + 6 Strap, Construction 20) are marked with their source; times, weights and min levels that no recovered source fixes are # ASSUMPTION and tunable here.

blueprints._skill_node_source: the construction tree's Workbench node (trees.json) is the learned blueprint gate; the historical 3 SP / Basic Workbench node is not in this tree yet
blueprints._work_seconds: # ASSUMPTION: spec 30 gives no build timer
blueprints.expected_level: # ASSUMPTION: floor(weighted average of level-contributing ingredients), clamped to [level_min, level_max] then capped by Construction

slots.label: Strap
slots._min_level: support slots add nothing to the level, so they must not gate it

blueprints._construction_level_source: historical tutorial building level (spec 30 section 2), the same gate the Basic Workbench carries
blueprints._footprint: the workbench grid kind: 2x1 cells for both the site and the finished station
blueprints._work_seconds: # ASSUMPTION: spec 29 gives no build timer

station._tags: spec 30 section 10: capabilities are data-driven tags. The finished center is a workbench-built station that also carries the comm_center tag, which is how CommCenter.built() and the save/restore find it (kind workbench is a kit-backed kind, so a reload rebuilds it instead of refunding it).
